clauses.reason: Terminated by statutory repeal on 1935-06-14. The operative lead approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Canning Industry subject to the two conditions. The order states no period, condition or date of its own, so it has no own-terms end. Its operative effect depended on section 3 of Title I: under 3(b) the approved code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade, a violation in or affecting interstate commerce was an unfair method of competition, under 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations and under 3(f) a violation was a misdemeanor. Section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 (49 Stat. 375, chapter 246, approved June 14, 1935) provides 'All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed' and states no later effective date, so the approval's prospective operative effect ended when the resolution was approved. Actor: the Congress by Senate Joint Resolution 113. The date is the resolution's approval date, not a general rule's default: the repeal reaches this command because the command had legal effect only through the repealed provisions. June 16, 1935 is not an end (section 1 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936). Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization recorded in source_notes, not an end date.

research_rationale:
Text and identity: EO 6729 is read in full in the registered American Presidency Project (APP) transcription jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6729-code-fair-competition-for-the-canning-industry.txt (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-29: the row with the same sha256 (03fb919b24d6...) in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl is a common-crawl capture (CC-MAIN-2025-43, captured 2025-10-17T18:39:17Z, WARC location recorded so the page can be re-fetched) whose heading is 'Executive Order 6729—Code of Fair Competition for the Canning Industry' and whose date is 1934-05-29; that date agrees with the date line of the held text ('May 29, 1934.'), and the row's text_sha256 equals the held file's. The held file is the whole order (recital, operative paragraph, signature, the Administrator's recommendation and the date line); it carries no order number, so the number comes from the page record. Clauses and sources are quoted from this registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. Identity: number, date and subject agree across the APP page record, the census register ('Executive Order 6729—Code of Fair Competition for the Canning Industry', 1934-05-29) and the WPA 1944 numbered list (printed page 580: 'Code of Fair Competition for the Canning Industry ap proved. XI NRA Codes 25.'). The text has a transcription slip in the recital ('clauses (1) and (a)' for '(1) and (2)') that does not affect the operative words; the WPA list adds the citation XI NRA Codes 25. EO 6729 (May 29, 1934, Franklin D. Roosevelt) adopts the Administrator's report, recommendations and findings and orders the Code of Fair Competition for the Canning Industry approved 'subject to the following conditions': (1) that the Industry designate a committee, subject to the Administrator's approval, to cooperate with the Administrator in formulating standards of quality and labelling requirements and 'to make recommendations to the Administrator within ninety (90) days' for inclusion in the code; and (a) that the Industry 'report not later than December 1, 1934 on the operation of the provisions of Articles III and IV with a view to improving the hour and wage provisions of this Code'. Legal reading: three clauses (the machine inventory is correct): the approval, the committee condition and the report condition. All three depend on section 3(a), which authorizes conditions of approval including 'requirements for the making of reports'. The approval has no period of its own. The conditions' ninety days (with no stated starting point) and December 1, 1934 are deadlines for recommendations and a report; they are not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadlines), and no held record shows whether the committee was designated or the report made. Each clause therefore ends with the repeal on 1935-06-14, which removed the approval these conditions qualify.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No own-terms end for the approval. For the committee condition and the report condition the stated periods are deadlines, not ends; the text gives no starting point for the ninety days, and no held record shows performance, so no earlier end is established for either. The name search found only this order within the range; the Canning and Packing Machinery Industry code (EO 6378 of October 31, 1933) is a different code. Searches made on 2026-10-29: (1) a full-text search of every held order text numbered 6200 through 7100 under jobs/*/output/texts (APP, HathiTrust GPO, Wikisource and Federal Register texts; clause-drafts copies excluded) for the code's name; (2) a citation search of the same texts for this order's number; (3) a search of the same texts for general NRA orders that could suspend, cancel or supersede codes: the held general orders (EO 6354 as amended by EO 6710, EO 6646, 6711, 6750-C, 6764 and 6829) prescribe rules, contract terms and delegations, and none suspends, cancels or supersedes the code named here; (4) the census register titles (jobs/domesday-register/output/REGISTER.csv) and the WPA 1944 numbered list, read for this code's name; they show no cancellation, suspension or superseding code. Orders for which no text is held (for example EO 6454) could not be searched, so the search covers held texts only. No held record shows this code cancelled or modified under section 10(b), superseded by another code, revoked or suspended before June 14, 1935. June 16, 1935 is not an end: it was Title I's original two-year expiry under section 2(c), which section 1 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 replaced with April 1, 1936. The approved code's own text is not held (it is printed in the NRA Codes volumes the WPA list cites), so a code-internal expiry or effective-date term could not be read; no held order records one for this code. Schechter (295 U.S. 495, May 27, 1935) is recorded in source_notes as a validity characterization, not as an end date: it reversed one conviction and held the Live Poultry Code provisions invalid, it did not cancel or withdraw this approving order, and no held record shows this code cancelled or suspended on that date.","independent_command_check":"Items (1) and (a) are conditions of the approval addressed to 'the Industry', to cooperate with the Administrator on standards for inclusion in this code and to report on the operation of this code's Articles III and IV; they are not appointments by the President, delegations under another statute or directions to an agency. The committee's membership 'shall be subject to the approval of the Administrator' but the order appoints no one. Each clause has its own end and its own deadline note.","savings_check":"Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code while the approval was in force are accrued effects, and the section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with the approved code taken while Title I was in effect (and for sixty days after) is an accrued effect for that completed action. The proviso to section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 narrows the exemption to agreements and action thereunder that put section 7(a) requirements into effect or prohibit practices already unlawful; it names agreements, states no time limit, and the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action under codes before June 14, 1935. No held source shows a prosecution continued after June 14, 1935, and none continues the approval itself. A committee designated or a report made before the repeal would be accrued, completed acts; no held source shows either, and nothing obliges either after the repeal.","scope_check":"Three clauses, as the machine inventory has them: the lead (approval 'subject to the following conditions'), item (1) and item (a). The recital, the signature, the Administrator's recommendation and the date line command nothing."}

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code while the approval was in force are accrued effects, and the section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with the approved code taken while Title I was in effect (and for sixty days after) is an accrued effect for that completed action. The proviso to section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 narrows the exemption to agreements and action thereunder that put section 7(a) requirements into effect or prohibit practices already unlawful; it names agreements, states no time limit, and the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action under codes before June 14, 1935. No held source shows a prosecution continued after June 14, 1935, and none continues the approval itself. A committee designated or a report made before the repeal would be accrued, completed acts; no held source shows either, and nothing obliges either after the repeal.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: Schechter, 295 U.S. 495: the judgment holds the code provisions in question invalid and reverses the conviction in No. 854; recorded with the syllabus and the delegation passage as a validity characterization of every section 3 code approval, not as an end date.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: Schechter opinion: 'We think that the code-making authority thus conferred is an unconstitutional delegation of legislative power.' The holding reaches section 3 approvals generally; it cancelled or withdrew no approving order.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: Schechter syllabus (No. 854: 'Argued May 2, 3, 1935.-Decided May 27, 1935'): supports the decision date recorded in the other Schechter notes.

source_notes.date_qualification: No event date: statutory text of June 16, 1933; the provisions delegating approval power and providing for code enforcement were repealed June 14, 1935.
source_notes.reason: NIRA section 3(a)-(f): the legal effects of a code approval that the repeal removed (3(a) approval and conditions, 3(b) standards of fair competition, 3(c) injunction suits, 3(f) misdemeanor).

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-06-16: not an end; section 1 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 replaced this expiry with April 1, 1936.
source_notes.reason: NIRA section 2(c): Title I's original two-year expiry, which fell on June 16, 1935.
